title: Seeing More, Better and Different: Ultrathin (UT) Membrane Chips for In-Situ/Operando Electron Microscopy
content: In-situ or operando electron microscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for studying fluid-solid interactions at high spatial resolution, contributing to important mechanistic understanding of phenomena in catalysis, energy storage, and environmental sciences [1]. The traditional encapsulation methods for in-situ EM with typical SiNx membranes (∼ 30-50 nm thick, on each side) introduce significant electron scattering and (chromatic) aberrations, thereby severely limiting spatial resolution and spectral visibility. Thus, a great number of advances in electron microscopy hardware and detectors are rendered less that effective because of these thickness limitations of conventional membranes. On the other end, methods such as graphene cell encapsulation may provide improved figures of merit but represent unique experiments, not conducive to round-robin type analysis or amenable to multimodal interrogation for cross validation.
